neighbours.label: a generic place or setting noun (place, spot, region) that completes a superlative or evaluative phrase ("the safest place", "the most beautiful regions")
fire: A noisy airport lounge is not the most pleasant place to hold a meeting.
For many birds the island is the safest place to build a nest.
The valley is one of the most fertile regions in the whole province.
A damp cellar is hardly the best place to keep old photographs.
The harbour is by far the liveliest place in town on a Saturday.
It was the most remote place the expedition had ever reached.
The delta is among the most productive regions for rice farming.
A dark cupboard is the worst place to dry wet boots.
quiet: The wedding took place in a noisy airport lounge.
In the first place, the island has no fresh water for nesting birds.
The valley has some of the most fertile soil in the whole province.
She put the old photographs back in place on the cellar shelf.
The harbour has by far the liveliest market in town on a Saturday.
It was the most remote village the expedition had ever reached.
Rice farming in the delta is among the most productive in Asia.
He finished in third place after drying his wet boots.

notes: Probes: 'most comfortable place' 0.63, 'most beautiful regions' 0.48, 'best time' 0.29, 'good way' 0.17; 'took place' 0.02, 'most beautiful paintings' 0.18. Time/way also appear in the top 32 but fired weaker, so the test is on place/region.
